items.prompt: The recursive contract is solve(i, remainingTarget), but the implementation caches results only by i. A solution note says, “The recursion repeats calls, so storing by index makes it a correct DP.” What is the best diagnosis?
constraints: The recurrence also carries a remaining target that changes future choices.
No proof of the index-only key is given.

options.text: The conclusion is unsupported: overlap exists, but the cache key omits a future-relevant state component and can merge different subproblems.
The reasoning is complete because any overlap guarantees a correct index-only DP.
The only possible issue is that memoization may be slower than tabulation.

feedback.reason: Repeated work is only one DP signal; the proposed index key is invalid because remaining target changes the unresolved problem.

blocks.text: A sound DP argument connects state meaning, complete identity, transition, bases, and evaluation. Here two calls at the same index can have different remaining targets and therefore different legal completions. Caching them together can return an answer from the wrong subproblem. The presence of overlap does not repair an incomplete state or prove the rest of the model.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.overlap_enough: Overlap identifies potential reuse, not which arguments define equality or whether the recurrence is correct.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.memo_speed_only: Performance is secondary; the omitted remaining target is a correctness defect in state identity.

items.prompt: A solver caches choose(i, remainingCapacity) only by i, and item i has weight 5. Which test most decisively exposes the bug?
constraints: At index i, the next item has weight 5 and positive value.

options.text: Compare i and i + 1 with the same capacity.
Run one large random input and check whether the final answer looks plausible.
Compare calls at the same i with capacities 4 and 5; the take branch is illegal in one and legal in the other.

feedback.reason: The capacities 4 and 5 create different legal futures under the same index key, directly refuting state sufficiency.

blocks.text: A diagnostic counterexample should isolate the omitted variable. At the same i, crossing the next item's weight threshold changes whether taking is possible, so the two correct suffix values can differ. An index-only cache cannot store both and will reuse whichever is computed first. This collision proof is smaller and more decisive than broad random testing.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.different_indices: Those calls already have different keys, so they do not demonstrate a collision in the proposed cache.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.large_random: A plausible final output may miss the defect; a minimal colliding pair directly proves the key merges nonequivalent states.

items.prompt: A memoized alignment solver returns correct values but is slower than a tabulation on dense inputs and can exhaust the recursion stack. What is the diagnosis?
constraints: The state, cache key, transition, and base cases have been verified correct.

options.text: The method is not dynamic programming because only a bottom-up table can evaluate a dense state space correctly.
The DP model is correct; dense reachability exposes top-down call, lookup, and stack overhead.
The state is incomplete because any correct memoized implementation must outperform an equivalent tabulation.

feedback.reason: Correctness and evaluation cost are separate dimensions; memoization is valid here but not the best operational choice.

blocks.text: The solver still evaluates each state consistently and returns the intended result. Dense reachability means top-down skips little work, while recursive calls, cache operations, and stack depth add costs that iterative loops may avoid. The repair is an implementation decision, not a new state or transition. Review should not mislabel every slower memoized solution as incorrect.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.state_bug: Runtime does not determine state sufficiency; verified correct outputs and state invariants separate this from a semantic defect.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.tabulation_only_dp: Memoized top-down evaluation is a valid DP implementation when it caches complete states and uses a correct recurrence.

items.prompt: A 0/1 capacity DP uses the correct one-array formula but processes capacity from low to high. Outputs match an unbounded-choice solution. What is the primary defect?
constraints: Each item should be used at most once.
The take term reads dp[c - w].

options.text: The loop reads current-item values after overwrite, changing the intended previous-layer dependency.
The base dp[0] must be wrong because update direction cannot change a recurrence's item multiplicity.
The recurrence lacks overlapping subproblems, so the one-array formula cannot represent dynamic programming.

feedback.reason: Ascending in-place updates alias the previous-item dependency with the current layer and permit repeated use.

blocks.text: The mathematical 0/1 recurrence reads values from the prior item layer. A descending loop preserves those values until consumption; an ascending loop overwrites lower capacities first and then reads them as if they were prior-layer states. The formula may look identical in code, but its operational meaning has changed. This is an iteration-order defect, not a base or overlap defect.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.base_only: The observed repeated use follows directly from ascending in-place updates even when dp[0] is correct.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.overlap_missing: Capacity states are reused; the problem is which version is read, not the absence of overlap.

items.prompt: A two-row DP returns the correct optimum length, but the API also requires one optimal alignment and no reconstruction plan exists. How should review classify it?
constraints: The discarded rows contained the ordinary predecessor trace.

options.text: The implementation is complete because a correct optimum scalar is sufficient evidence of an optimal alignment.
The recurrence is incorrect because any valid alignment recurrence must retain the full value table.
The value computation is correct, but the required witness has no retained or recomputable trace.

feedback.reason: The optimized storage satisfies only the value subproblem, not the complete witness-producing contract.

blocks.text: Review should separate forward value correctness from output completeness. Rolling rows can preserve every dependency needed to compute the optimum while discarding the history used to recover an alignment. Without parent data, checkpoints, or recomputation, the API cannot deliver its required witness. This is a compression/output-boundary defect, not proof that the recurrence itself is wrong.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.fully_correct: The stated API requires a witness, so satisfying only a narrower scalar contract is insufficient.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.wrong_recurrence: The value recurrence can remain correct; the defect is information loss relative to reconstruction.

items.prompt: Order a disciplined DP mistake review using a small counterexample and an uncompressed reference.
constraints: The reference recurrence and expected state meanings are trusted.
The implementation exposes state values or a trace.

elements.text: Reduce the failing input while preserving the wrong result.
Verify every reachable base and impossible-state sentinel on that input.
Compare states in dependency order and identify the first value that diverges.
Inspect that state's inputs, transition, and update versions to classify the defect before changing code.

feedback.reason: The first divergent state is the narrowest point at which a wrong base, transition, or dependency version can enter the computation.

blocks.text: Find the first state where correctness is lost

items: Minimize the failing input while preserving the wrong result so fewer states and branches remain.
Verify every reachable base and impossible-state sentinel against the state meaning.
Compare the implementation with the uncompressed reference in dependency order and locate the first divergent state.
Inspect that state’s inputs, transition and logical value versions to classify the defect before editing code.

blocks.text: At the first divergence, earlier dependencies should still match the reference, which isolates the local base, transition or update-version error. Editing before classification can mask one defect with another.

blocks.title: Diagnostic order
blocks.text: Minimize input → verify bases → find first divergent state → classify its broken contract.

items.prompt: Select all defect-to-owner mappings that are correct.
constraints: Each defect is described at its first violated contract.

options.text: Two histories share a cache key but have different legal futures → define_dp_state.
A blocked origin is seeded with one path → define_transition.
A one-row update reads a current-layer value where the recurrence requires a previous layer → iteration_order.
The optimum value is correct but no witness can be recovered → recognize_overlapping_subproblems.

feedback.reason: Diagnosis should name the first broken contract and route the repair to its owning mental unit.

blocks.text: State collisions are repaired by defining a sufficient state or key. Wrong-layer reads arise from an evaluation order that does not preserve the recurrence's dependency versions. A blocked-origin seed is a base feasibility error, while a missing witness is a reconstruction/storage-output issue. This ownership discipline keeps mistake review diagnostic rather than turning it into a second, overlapping version of every DP lesson.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.base_as_transition: The first violated contract is feasibility of the terminal/start state, so base_cases_and_initialization owns the repair.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.reconstruct_as_overlap: The defect concerns preserved predecessor evidence and output reconstruction, not whether equal states recur.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.state_owner: A cache collision between nonequivalent histories is a state-sufficiency defect.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.order_owner: Reading the wrong logical layer is an iteration/update-order defect.

items.prompt: A minimization DP initializes unreachable states to 0 and returns an implausibly cheap route through blocked cells. What defect owner should review first?

options.text: Base-case and impossible-state initialization: unavailable states must not compete as zero-cost candidates.
Variable naming, because the loop may read the wrong symbolic names.
Memoization itself, even if every state is computed from the wrong initial values.
Output formatting, because the numeric minimum is already determined correctly.

feedback.reason: A zero sentinel changes the recurrence's feasible set before transitions or caching can be evaluated.

blocks.text: The first review target is the meaning of unreachable states and the neutral element for minimization. A cache can faithfully reuse a wrong zero; changing memoization without fixing initialization preserves the defect. The symptom is a semantic base/transition boundary issue, not formatting.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.loop_language: Names do not explain a false zero-cost route.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.memo_cache_only: Caching incorrect base values reproduces the same wrong answer efficiently.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.output_format: The numeric state is already wrong before it is rendered.

items.prompt: A DP returns the correct optimum value but cannot return the required chosen items because its compressed state stores no decisions. Which defect classification is precise?

options.text: The value recurrence is correct, but state compression lost witness information required by the output contract.
The numeric objective must be wrong because no path was reconstructed.
The issue is necessarily the empty-input base case.
Only runtime is affected; a missing witness is not a correctness defect.

feedback.reason: An algorithm can compute the scalar optimum correctly while failing a separate witness-output requirement.

blocks.text: Review should separate value correctness from reconstruction completeness. Parent pointers, retained decisions, checkpoints, or a recoverable reference computation can repair the output contract, but merely recomputing a scalar does not identify the selected items. The defect belongs to compression/reconstruction ownership.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.wrong_objective: The stated value is correct; the missing part is the witness.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.base_case_only: No evidence points to an empty-input boundary; the failure is information loss during compression.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.time_complexity_only: Missing required output is a correctness/contract defect, not merely a performance concern.

items.prompt: A memo key includes index and capacity, but the transition uses dp(i, capacity - weight[i]) even when the item does not fit. Which review order is most useful?

options.text: Review branch legality and transition preconditions first; the state dimensions may be sufficient while the recurrence admits an invalid take.
Add every local variable to the memo key before checking whether the transition is legal.
Replace DP with a greedy method because every transition bug proves DP is unsuitable.
Ignore the branch because memoization will cache the invalid state consistently.

feedback.reason: The key can be complete while a branch still violates the problem's feasibility predicate.

blocks.text: State sufficiency and transition legality are separate review owners. If weight[i] exceeds capacity, the take branch must be excluded or marked impossible; adding arbitrary key fields does not repair it. Caching a wrong successor only makes the invalid recurrence faster.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.add_more_key_fields: No memo key can make an illegal transition legal; first check the recurrence's guard.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.switch_to_greedy: A local transition defect does not establish that the DP model is inappropriate.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.ignore_if_cached: Consistency of a cached wrong state is not correctness.

items.prompt: A DP passes simple tests but fails when capacity changes; the table is keyed only by index. What is the likely defect?

options.text: The state omits a future-relevant capacity dimension, merging different subproblems.
The base case has too many dimensions.
Any loop with a capacity is necessarily invalid.
The table uses too much memory, which directly causes wrong values.

feedback.reason: Different remaining capacities expose different legal choices and need different DP results.

blocks.text: A small counterexample with the same index and two capacities can expose the collision. Add the missing dimension before attempting space compression.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.base-too-large: The problem is missing state, not excessive base coverage.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.iteration-too-fast: A capacity loop can be correct when it follows dependencies.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.memory-too-much: Space pressure is separate from semantic state completeness.

items.prompt: A counting DP returns a maximum instead of the number of constructions. Which defect is present?

options.text: The transition uses an optimization operator instead of summing legal alternatives.
The state contains too much information, so counts become maxima.
The table needs sorted indices before addition.
Counting and optimization always use the same operator.

feedback.reason: The recurrence's combine operator must match the output semantic.

blocks.text: A count aggregates all legal branches; a max selects one best branch. State and iteration order may be correct while the operator is wrong.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.state-too-large: State size does not determine whether branches are summed or optimized.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort-needed: DP addition does not require sorting indices.

items.prompt: A rolling-array DP gives wrong values after in-place compression. What should be inspected first?

options.text: Whether the loop overwrites a predecessor before all transitions that need its old value have read it.
Whether the array variable has a descriptive name.
Whether input values are sorted after compression.
Whether every state was initialized to one.

feedback.reason: Compression changes storage aliasing and can destroy a dependency before it is consumed.

blocks.text: Choose forward or reverse iteration from the transition direction, or retain two rows when one row cannot safely represent both old and new states.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.table-name: Names do not affect state dependencies.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.base-count: A universal one base is not correct for every DP.

items.prompt: A DP fails only on impossible states because infinity plus a transition cost becomes a finite wrapped value. What is wrong?

options.text: The unreachable sentinel is being used in arithmetic without guarding it or choosing a safe representation.
The recurrence has too many overlapping subproblems.
The input must be sorted before adding costs.
The issue is that count DP should start at zero.

feedback.reason: An unreachable marker must remain distinguishable from every legal finite result through transitions.

blocks.text: Guard transitions from unreachable predecessors or use a wide sentinel with overflow-safe checks. Base values and arithmetic domain belong to the same correctness contract.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.overlap-proof: Overlap affects work, not sentinel arithmetic.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort-order: Cost transitions do not require sorted input.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.count-zero: This is an optimization-state sentinel defect, not a count identity choice.

contrastSets.transferBoundary: Repeated complete states justify reuse, but state sufficiency, recurrence correctness, and terminal semantics remain separate proofs.
An index is sufficient only when no independent resource, coordinate, or history feature changes future behavior.
Top-down can skip unreachable states; dense state spaces may favor bottom-up locality and lower call overhead.
The recurrence defines dependency edges; the schedule must respect the logical version of every dependency.
Compression must preserve dependency versions and every output consumer, including witness reconstruction.
